# Challenge and field scan: Hacktoberfest Week 1 "Touch Grass"

Snapshot: Saturday 2026-10-10, entries published up to 16:46 UTC. The deadline is about 38 hours later.

## The challenge

Source: DEV event 79, read through DevRelay `get_challenge_details`, plus the launch post and the HF26 hub.

- Launch post: https://dev.to/devteam/join-the-hacktoberfest-open-source-ai-challenge-week-1-touch-grass-2450-in-prizes-across-17-4pom
- Challenge page: https://dev.to/challenges/hacktoberfest-week1-2026-10-05
- Hub with category rules: https://dev.to/challenges/hf26

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Prompt | Build something with open-source AI at its core that gets people off the screen and into the world. |
| Bar the organizers set | "The best builds here should make the screen the shortest part of the experience." |
| Bonus | Take it outside, use it, and tell us how it went. |
| Post must explain | Why open innovation matters for what you built, and where open beat closed. |
| Deadline | Sun Oct 11, 11:59 PM PDT = Mon Oct 12, 06:59 UTC = 2:59 AM ET. API `ends_at` is `2026-10-12T06:59:00Z`. |
| Required | A DEV post using the official template, tag `#hf26challenge`. New project built in the window (Oct 5 to Oct 11). One entry per person. Teams up to 4, one post, list teammates' DEV handles. |
| Later commits | Allowed only if noted in the README. Unnoted ones risk disqualification. |
| Judging | Writing Quality (weighted most), Relevance, Creativity, Technical Execution, Use of Partner Technology (optional). |
| Ties | Broken by positive reactions on the post. |
| Prizes | Overall $250 + DEV++ + badge. 6 featured categories at $200. 10 partner categories at $100. 17 winners. One win per person per challenge. |
| Agent session | Optional. "Judges love it." Save with DevRelay, embed with the `agent_session` tag. Uploads are unlisted by default, so make them public and scrub keys. |

A DEV staff member said in the launch post comments that people may submit by their own local time (comment 3ghbj, by heyitsjem). The rules make the sponsor's clock official. For us in ET, 06:59 UTC is later than local midnight anyway, so plan to the UTC time.

### Template sections, in order

1. Opening line: "This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass" (with the challenge link)
2. What I Built (what it does, how it gets people outside, who it's for)
3. Demo (deployed link or video)
4. Code (GitHub embed)
5. How I Built It (which open-source AI, and how the project is built around it)
6. Why Does Open Innovation Matter?
7. My Agent Session (optional)
8. Prize Categories (list each one, or remove)

Front matter tags in the template: `devchallenge, hf26challenge`.

### Category rules that matter to our stack

From the hub page:

- **Gemma ($200):** use Gemma, run it locally, fine-tune it, or serve it through Google Cloud or another provider.
- **Render ($200):** use Render as the AI runtime, host an agent's front end, or run Hermes or OpenClaw.
- **MongoDB Atlas ($100):** Atlas as the data layer, Atlas Vector Search for retrieval, agent memory, or the database behind an app on an open-weight model.
- **Entire ($100):** share the agent sessions behind the project in the write-up, or search past agent work to explain why code exists.
- **ElevenLabs ($100):** give an open-source agent a voice, transcribe audio for a local model, or narrate the demo.
- **Sentry Agent Tracing ($100):** show setup, latency, tokens, cost, what you found and how you debugged it, with traces or screenshots.

Every entry is judged for every category it qualifies for. Partner credits (Render, Tinker, Backboard, ElevenLabs) are claimed at hacktoberfest.com/my/promos.

## The field

### Method

1. **Listing.** Merged three sources, because DEV's paged API skips and repeats posts as their order shifts (see BUG-001 in docs/BUGLOG.md):
   - DevRelay `get_articles` for the tag, 10 pages of 100
   - DevRelay `execute_dev_api_request` with `top`, 9 pages of 100
   - DEV's date-sorted search feed (`/search/feed_content`), which caps at 800 results per sort direction, run newest-first and oldest-first

   The union holds 2,009 `#hf26challenge` posts. Week 1 entries are those published from Oct 5 07:00 UTC on, without the `weekendchallenge` tag or the Weekend template line. **That leaves 813 entries.** All 48 most-reacted Week 1 posts are in the set. The only gap is Oct 5, 18:00 to 20:58 UTC, the first three hours after launch, which has 7 posts in the set.
2. **Text.** Pulled the article text of all 813 from the CDN-served pages, cut at the end of the article body, with HTML comments stripped (the template's comments mention DevRelay and agent sessions). On three spot checks the extracted text was within 1 to 7% of the original markdown's word count.
3. **Counting.** Counted keyword matches in the title and article text. A keyword match is not proof of use, and the prompt's own examples ("bird call", "run club") inflate some themes. Theme counts use titles only, which is stricter. Small counts (quorum, accessibility, Telegram) were checked by hand.
4. **Reactions.** From DEV API `GET /api/articles?tag=hf26challenge&top=7`.
5. **Reading.** Two research passes read the top 15 Week 1 entries and all 17 Weekend winners in full. Their findings are in the last two sections.

180	# ADR-0027: ElevenLabs for a warm compass voice and Voice Spark
181	
182	Status: Accepted (Sun 2026-10-11).
183	
184	## Context
185	Flare's compass talks so a friend who can't look at the screen (low vision, bright sun, hands busy) can still find the group (SRS-CMP-1). It used the phone's built-in voice, which on many phones sounds flat or robotic. The founder asked for ElevenLabs as the signature voice, with two limits: use it only to voice text Flare itself generates, plus an opt-in way for a person to say their own Spark. Never record group conversations: the people around you didn't agree to it, and Flare's promise is that it leaves nothing behind.
186	
187	The ElevenLabs account is on the free tier: 10,000 characters a month (0 used when this was written), 3 custom voices, premade voices available.
188	
189	## Decision
190	
191	### 1. Warm voice for the compass: recorded once, shipped as files
192	- **What it says.** A fixed set of 54 short lines from the copy deck, recorded once by `scripts/gen-voice.ts` into `apps/web/static/voice/` with a manifest:
193	  - distances: 5 to 95 m in steps of 5, 100 to 950 m in steps of 50, and 1 to 5 km;
194	  - directions: slightly left/right, to your left/right, behind you;
195	  - other lines: "Straight ahead.", "You're close. Look around.", hold flat, no GPS, and figure 8.
196	- **No names.** The lines never include the friend's or the spot's name. A spoken compass line that includes a place name would have to send that name to ElevenLabs at run time. These clips leave that out, and the name stays on screen.
197	- **Cost and size.** 698 characters, once: 7% of a month's free allowance. 54 MP3 files at 64 kbps, 684 KB in all. A re-run keeps existing clips and spends nothing.
198	- **Opt-in on this phone.** My needs now has a Warm voice choice and a "Hear it" sample. Turning it on stores `flare.voice=warm` and saves every clip in the Cache API (`flare-voice-1`), so it works with no signal. Turning it off deletes that cache. The clips stay off the service-worker precache.
199	- **Playback.** `lib/compass/voice.ts`:
200	  - `clipsFor()` maps the compass state to one or two clips, for example `["m-150", "dir-slightLeft"]`.
201	  - `playWarm()` plays them in order from the cache.
202	  - The phone's own voice is the fallback when a clip is missing or audio can't play.
203	  - The player loads only on phones that turned the warm voice on, which keeps it inside the 150 KB JS budget.
204	  - The repeat rules stay the same (SRS-CMP-2).
205	- **Server.** `.mp3` is now served as `audio/mpeg`. The CSP is `media-src 'self' blob:`, because cached clips play as blob URLs.
206	
207	### 2. Voice Spark: your own words, said instead of typed
208	- **When it's offered.** "Say it" appears on the Spark screen only when `/config` reports `voice.spark: true`, which needs `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` on the server, and only when the browser can record.
209	- **Recording.** One tap starts it and a second tap stops it. It stops by itself at 10 s and shows a countdown. Tapping suits more people than hold-to-talk. The microphone is released the moment recording stops.
210	- **What the server does.** `POST /api/v1/voice/spark` accepts audio types only, up to 400 KB. It sends the clip once to ElevenLabs Scribe (`scribe_v2`, English, no audio-event tags) and returns `{text}`, at most 140 characters. The buffer is zero-filled in a `finally` block. Nothing is stored or logged.
211	- **Failures and limits.** A 503 means the server has no key. `text: null` means Scribe failed, and the person types instead. The server caps transcriptions at `VOICE_SPARK_DAILY_MAX` a day (default 40).
212	- **After the words come back.** They land in the text field for the person to edit. The Spark is then sealed on the phone as before. The "no AI help" rule (BR-K-1 to K-3) still holds, because this only writes down the person's own words.
213	
214	### 3. What we will not do
215	- Record anyone other than the person who tapped.
216	- Listen in the background, or record a gathering or a conversation.
217	- Send ElevenLabs a name, a place, an invite or anything sealed.
218	
219	## Privacy
220	- The privacy page gains `site.privacy.l.voice`:
221	  - the compass voice ships with the app and sends nothing;
222	  - Say it sends up to 10 s of your own voice once, after you tap;
223	  - Flare keeps no audio;
224	  - ElevenLabs may keep it under its own terms.
225	- ElevenLabs is the one closed API in Flare's voice path. Its zero-retention mode is an enterprise feature, so we don't claim it.
226	
227	## Measured (2026-10-11)
228	- **Clips.** Generating all 54 used 698 characters. Each clip is 1 to 2 s long; "You're close. Look around." is 1.5 s.
229	- **Scribe on our own clips.** It returned "You're close. Look around" in 492 ms and "150 meters" in 420 ms, both word for word (scribe_v2; scribe_v1 matched).
230	
231	## Tests
232	- `apps/web/test/flow/voice.test.ts`: distance rounding, directions, facing, near, no heading and no GPS map to the right clips. Every clip the compass can ask for exists and matches the generator's buckets. No clip text holds anything but fixed words.
233	- `apps/server/test/voice.test.ts`: off without a key (503, and `/config` says false); Scribe gets the person's audio with the key in a header; non-audio is refused (415); over 400 KB is refused (413); a Scribe failure returns `text: null`; the daily cap holds.
234	- `apps/web/test/e2e/sparks.ts`: in Chrome, "Say it" records a real MediaRecorder clip from a synthetic microphone, sends `audio/webm` once, and the words land in the field to edit. Headless Chrome hangs on audio-only `getUserMedia`, so the test gives that page a tone as its microphone.
235	
236	## Consequences
237	- The compass has a warm voice that works offline and costs nothing per use.
238	- A person can say their Spark. That sends their own voice to one closed service, only when they tap, and the privacy page says so.
239	- Adding a new compass line now means adding a deck key, adding a clip id in `gen-voice.ts` and `voice.ts`, and running `node scripts/gen-voice.ts`. The unit test catches a clip that is missing.

249	- **Ollama reports audio.** For `gemma4:e4b-it-q4_K_M`, Ollama 0.40.2 lists the capabilities `completion, vision, audio, tools, thinking` (`/api/show`).
250	- **Audio goes in `images`.** The model hears audio passed base64 in a message's `images` field. A field named `audio` is ignored.
251	- **Transcription works.** One of our own warm-voice clips came back as "You're close. Look around." in 2 s.
252	- **The voice prompt works.** Voice prompt v1, given a `say` recording of "I'm at the pond in Ford Woods Park. Come sit on the bench with me, the light is really nice.", answered `{"invite": "Meet at the pond bench.", "alt": "The pond in Fordwoods Park has nice light to sit on the bench."}` in 3.7 s. A second sentence ("Walk to the cider mill after work? I'm by the big oak at Fairlane Green.") took 3.5 s.
253	
254	## Decision
255	- **Phone.** The camera screen has "Say it instead".
256	  - One tap starts recording and a second tap stops it. It stops by itself at 10 s.
257	  - The phone converts the clip to 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV (`lib/voice/flare.ts`) and sends it once to `POST /api/v1/drafts/voice`.
258	  - Nothing is kept on the phone, and the microphone is released at once.
259	  - The control loads only when the camera screen shows (JS budget).
260	- **Server.** WAV only (RIFF....WAVE), at most 400 KB.
261	  - It relays the audio to the hub as a `voice-draft` job (asyncapi `voiceJob`: a header, then one binary frame) with an 8 s budget, like the ladder.
262	  - It runs `enforce()` again on the answer.
263	  - The buffer is zero-filled on every path, and nothing is stored or logged.
264	  - The words heard never come back, only `{invite, alt, tier}`.
265	  - It counts `tier_ran.voice.{tier}`.
266	- **No cloud tier.** A voice is more personal than a photo, so it stays on the open model on our own laptop. If the hub is absent, slow or hears no place, the response is `tier: rules`. The phone then says "Didn't catch a place. Take a photo or try again."
267	- **Hub.** The frame must start with RIFF, or the result is `bad_audio` and the model is never called. The hub uses voice prompt v1 (`packages/shared/src/prompts/voice.ts`): only places and things the person said, no names, faces or bodies, and an empty answer when no place is heard. It runs `enforce()` and makes no retry: at temperature 0 a retry gives the same answer. The audio is zero-filled after the job.
268	- **Send.** With no photo, Send shows the invite over the outdoor scenery and asks for the place if the map didn't name one.
269	
270	## Tests
271	- `apps/hub/test/voice.test.ts`:
272	  - audio in, a guarded draft out, with the voice prompt and the audio passed as media;
273	  - an empty answer is `unusable_answer`;
274	  - a frame that isn't WAV is `bad_audio` and never reaches the model.
275	- `apps/server/test/contract.test.ts` (`draftFromVoice`): the template when no hub is connected, 400 for a file that isn't WAV, 413, and 415.
276	- `apps/web/test/e2e/voice-flare.ts` runs on the real stack on this Mac: real server, real hub, real Gemma 4.
277	  - The `say` fixture plays in as the microphone. A real MediaRecorder records it and the phone converts it to WAV (167 KB).
278	  - "Meet at the pond bench" comes back in 3.3 s, and Send shows it over the scenery with no photo.
279	
280	## Consequences
281	- A person who can't take a photo can still send a Flare by speaking for 10 seconds, and their voice goes only to our own laptop.
282	- Asyncapi gains `voiceJob` and `voiceBytes`, and the result error enum gains `bad_audio`. A hub on the old code ignores the job, and the server falls back to the template after 8 s.

284	# ADR-0029: Crew Atlas, your crew's places drawn on the phone
285	
286	Status: Accepted (Sun 2026-10-11).
287	
288	## Context
289	The backlog (#9) asked for a Crew Atlas: the crew's outings, Sparks and Hot spots as a private map of its places, with facts that come only from data. The crew's places live in the sealed Hot spots blob, which only members' phones can open. Each entry has the place key (an OSM id from the map pack), the name, how many times the crew met there and the last day, and no coordinates.
290	
291	## Decision
292	- **Drawing.** The Atlas is drawn on the phone (`lib/components/CrewAtlas.svelte`) at the top of the Crew space, when the crew has places.
293	  - **Positions** come from the map pack already on the phone: `place_key` → `items[3]` → lat and lon. Typed places with no OSM id are listed but not drawn.
294	  - **Context** comes from the same pack: water, woods, parks, streets and benches inside the box, at most 1,200 points.
295	  - **Nothing is fetched for it.** There are no map tiles and no requests, so where the crew meets never leaves the phone. The only network use is the pack file, which the app already loads.
296	- **Facts only from data.** "Met once · Oct 11" or "Met 3 times · last Oct 4", from the blob's count and last day. Dot size grows with the count, at 6 + 3·log2(count) px.
297	- **No AI caption.** The backlog imagined Gemma writing the Atlas. Gemma runs on the hub, so a written caption would mean sending the crew's decrypted places off the phone, which breaks the Hot spots promise (BR-K-6). The facts read just as well from templates, so we left the model out.
298	- **Accessibility.** The SVG is `role="img"` with a label ("Map of 3 places your crew met"), and the list of facts underneath carries the same information as text.
299	- **Budget.** The component and the map module load on demand from the Crew page.
300	
301	## Tests
302	`apps/web/test/e2e/sparks.ts` runs on the real stack. It creates a real Hot spot: a Flare lights, a friend arrives, and the host ends it. The Crew page then shows the Atlas with "West Road · Met once · Oct 11" (`docs/frontend/evidence/e2e-crew-atlas.png`).
303	
304	## Consequences
305	- The crew gets a map of where it goes outside, private by construction.
306	- When a crew uses more than one map pack, the Atlas draws the places found in the pack named by `area`, which is Fairlane by default.

309	
310	Status: Accepted (Sun 2026-10-11).

313	
314	| Automation | Status | How |
315	| --- | --- | --- |
316	| Plan auto-solve at the deadline | Already there | The engine's `plan_deadline` job; the server sweeps every 60 s and at boot (ADR-0005) |
317	| Fade check, "still coming?" | Already there | `still_coming` push when a Plan gets smaller (BR-P-6) |
318	| Locked Plan saved for offline use | Already there | PWA outbox and saved view (`savedAt`) |
319	| **Reminder 30 min before a Plan starts** | **New** | When a Plan lights more than 30 min before its start, the engine schedules `plan_reminder` at start − 30 min. The timer pushes `plan_soon` to the people going: "{step} starts at {time}. Time to head out." The text is built on the phone from the sealed notice, so the server sees only the event name. The job is unscheduled when the Plan ends. Migration 0005 allows the new job kind |
320	| **Weather-aware Ember** | **New** | When Home's 2-hour forecast says rain is likely, the host's phone puts covered seats first in the Ember list. A seat counts as covered if it is tagged `covered=yes` or `shelter=yes`, or is within 25 m of a mapped shelter. The engine picks the first seat everyone passed, and that seat's name reads "the bench by the willow, under cover", so friends see why. All on the phone; the server never learns the weather or the spot |
321	| **Tell the chat** | **New** | On the host's Lit screen, one tap opens the share sheet (or copies) with "It is lit. Meet us at {spot}." and the same link as the invite. A place only, never who |
322	| Golden-hour nudge (a push) | Not built | Home already shows "Golden hour in 47 min" with one tap to Light a Flare. A push at golden hour would need the server to know where each crew is, which it never does (ADR-0001). A local notification at a set time isn't available to web apps without push |
323	| Weekly recap (a push or Telegram post) | Not built | The Crew space already shows this week's minutes outside from the counters (ADR-0024). A pushed recap needs a weekly job per crew at a sensible local hour, and the server doesn't know a crew's time zone. Left for after the challenge |

329	  - Tell the chat sends nothing until the host shares it.

344	# ADR-0031: Remember this, a conversation note made only with everyone's consent
345	
346	Status: Accepted (Sun 2026-10-11, founder decision). Replaces ADR-0027's "never record a conversation" with the rule below.
347	
348	## The rule
349	- **Per Flare or Plan, off by default.** The host turns it on (`PUT /remember {on}`), and it is never on for a crew all the time. Turning it off clears every consent and any recording.
350	- **Each person agrees on their own phone,** separately from I'm in (`PUT /remember/consent {ok}`).
351	  - If anyone who said yes doesn't agree, it's off for everyone.
352	  - If someone joins later without agreeing, it's off for everyone.
353	  - The screen says "Recording is off for this Flare." and never who. That's the same rule as the yes count.
354	  - The rule is one pure function, `rememberState()` in `apps/server/src/core/remember.ts`. It returns flags only: `on`, `ready`, `recording`, `recording_until`.
355	- **Recording.** When it's lit and everyone agreed, anyone can tap Record. It records up to 60 s on that phone, after the line "Only your group. Stop if others are close." Every phone in the group shows a recording sign, live (SSE event `remember`). Anyone can stop it for everyone, and a no stops it at once.
356	- **The words.** ElevenLabs Scribe v2, `diarize=true`, turns the audio into lines labelled Speaker 1, Speaker 2 and so on, with no names. The audio is zero-filled right after the call and none is kept. ElevenLabs may keep it under its own terms, and the privacy page says so.
357	- **The note.** The lines go back to the recording phone, which seals them with the Flare key (aad `r:{gathering}`). The server stores only that sealed blob, so it never holds the words in plain text.
358	- **The summary.** Gemma on the hub writes one line: summary prompt v1, `enforceSummary()` on the hub and on the server (3 to 16 words, no speaker labels, no long numbers or links). With the hub off there's no summary, and the words never go to a cloud model.
359	- **Where it shows.** The note shows in the Remember this sheet while the gathering is live. It is deleted at Gone with everything else: both tables cascade with the gathering, and the deletion audit checks them as DS12.
360	- **Never** listens in the background, and never records without the host turning it on and everyone agreeing.
361	
362	## Measured (this Mac, 2026-10-11)
363	- **Scribe on a 10 s, two-voice `say` clip:** 787 ms direct and 720 ms through the app. Two speakers, labels only.
364	- **End to end:** stop tap → transcription → hub summary → sealed note shown on the other phone: 5.3 s. Gemma's line: "Friends enjoyed the beautiful view of the pond and geese together."
365	
366	## Tests
367	- `apps/server/test/remember.test.ts`, properties with fast-check:
368	  - ready exactly when on, lit and every yes agreed;
369	  - any no makes it off for everyone;
370	  - a late joiner without consent makes it off;
371	  - the result never holds a member id, and doesn't depend on order;
372	  - recording only while ready and inside its 60 s.
373	  - Also covered: the transcript lines and the summary guard.
374	- `apps/server/test/contract.test.ts`: host-only on; consent; a no stops a recording; stop for everyone; the sealed note; 503 without ElevenLabs; no hub means no summary; 409 when not everyone agreed. No member id appears in any answer.
375	- `apps/web/test/e2e/remember.ts`, on the real stack with two phones:
376	  - the host turns it on and the friend agrees on their own phone;
377	  - the sign shows live on the other phone, and the friend stops it for everyone;
378	  - a real Scribe call and the real hub summary;
379	  - the note reaches the other phone with speaker labels and no names.

# ADR-0023: Telegram posts show a branded card; real photos only on a group opt-in

Status: Accepted (founder decision, Sun 2026-10-11 ~06:40 ET). Amends ADR-0013 (Telegram groups) and contracts/telegram.md section 3.

## Context
ADR-0013 posted the Flare photo to Telegram when the host's phone sent it, else plain text. The phone never sent it, so every post was text. The founder wants Telegram to look like Flare, and wants the real photo there only when a group chooses it, because a Telegram post is the one place a Flare's content leaves our encryption.

## Decision
- **Default: a branded card.** The bot posts a 1200x800 PNG rendered on the server in memory (`apps/server/src/telegram/card.ts`): the flame for the state (Kindling grows with the count, Lit with the gold dot, Ember's dome, Gone's smoke), the six words, the place label the caption already shows, and the count line. No host or member names, no real photo, no location beyond the place label. The caption and buttons are unchanged (telegram.md 3).
- **The card follows the state.** Every edit of a card post is `editMessageMedia` with a newly drawn card and the new caption: count changes, Lit, Ember, Smaller plan, and the final line. Every bot message is still deleted at Gone (telegram.md 6, BR-D-3).
- **Real photo: per group, off by default.** `groups.telegram_photos` (migration 0004), set from the phone's "Post in Telegram" screen through `PUT /groups/{id}/telegram-settings`. Only when it is on does the host's phone send the Flare's 768 px JPEG with `PUT /gatherings/{id}/telegram-photo`. The server uploads it with `sendPhoto` from memory, zero-fills the buffer and keeps nothing. With it off, that route answers 409 and the bot does not wait for a photo. A real-photo post edits only its caption.
- **Disclosure, in three places:** the setting itself ("Telegram keeps a copy until the post is deleted; everyone in the group sees it."), the privacy page (`site.privacy.l.telegram`), and this ADR. Groups that use links only are unaffected.
- **Rendering stack:** `@resvg/resvg-wasm` 2.6.2 (published 2024-03, MPL-2.0; WASM, so the same on the Mac and on Render) with the website's fontsource faces. resvg reads TTF/OTF, so the WOFF 1.0 files are unpacked in memory (`woff.ts`, about 50 lines). We did not use satori: it had about a dozen releases in the three days before this decision, too new to trust for a release candidate.

## Consequences
- The card costs 15 to 60 ms of CPU per post or edit; edits stay coalesced to one per 3 s per message (telegram.md 5).
- If the card cannot be rendered, the post falls back to text with the same caption and buttons.
- After a server restart the bot does not know whether a post was a card or a photo; it then edits the caption only, which is correct for both.

## Proof
- Server tests: card PNG size, no host name in the card, state views, the app's flame geometry, WOFF conversion; photos off by default, 409 when off, card at once, card after the wait when on, edits by `editMessageMedia`, deletion at Gone (`apps/server/test/integrations/telegram*.test.ts`, 178 server tests pass).
- Real stack, phone to fake Bot API: `npm run e2e:telegram`, 14/14 (card PNG with caption and three buttons; photo on gives the host's JPEG).
